title: PTSIP customer common contracts — Go implementation and Python-feature migration

scope.user_intent: Build customer-owned six-schema common contract capability in Go; remove replaced Python customer contract feature; preserve independent developer extension contracts and installed package resource access.

work_units.title: Inventory precise current call sites and approved authority
actions: Build exact call graph with imports, build-time invocation, source restoration, contract validation, and installed package consumers; do not infer ownership from file names.
Snapshot existing unified source roundtrip and developer policy document verification before modification.
Classify functions to replace in Go, build-time adapters, and unrelated Python code that remains out of scope.
Separate 0.3.8 release control plane and unadmitted Plan schema constraints from this plan.
outputs: Machine-readable impact inventory: current caller, owned behavior, replacement entrypoint, required regression, exact owner.
Behavior parity corpus and approved-policy revision binding.
acceptance: All known direct or indirect callers accounted for before any deletion.
No change to unrelated official engine behavior or SFP/MPD policy authority.

work_units.title: Declare customer-owned six schemas, 13-status lifecycle and exact-version URNs
actions: Create independent JSON Schema documents for all six resources under src/ptsip/common_contract/schemas/ as development sources, never as fixed customer runtime paths.
Define customer Policy Lifecycle's own exactly thirteen official enum values without referencing .ptsip developer contracts.
Define schema identities and version registration data, preserving flexible customer extension fields and rejecting invented mandatory customer fields.
Introduce explicit contract metadata where logical semantics cannot be inferred from property names.
outputs: Six versioned JSON schemas.
Installed-package-relative resource mappings and resource manifest.
13-status validation fixtures.
acceptance: All six resources have unique registered exact-version URNs and resolvable installed-package names.
All thirteen official statuses accepted by customer lifecycle contract.
No import/$ref from customer schemas to developer-only contracts.
Unapproved extra universal required fields and unrelated restriction not introduced.

work_units.title: Implement standalone Go package-resource registry and resolution
actions: Implement Go module rooted at src/ptsip/common_contract/ independent of .ptsip/engine/developer.
Split Go packages by registry, resource lookup, reference resolution, validation, compatibility and command adapter.
Build version-bound URN resolution, duplicate-ID rejection, cycles and missing reference reporting.
Provide machine-readable request and response contracts. For the installed binary, resolve package resources relative to the installed PTSIP package rather than a fixed checkout or venv location.
Ensure Windows, Linux, macOS binaries can locate the installed registry and schemas without developer engine or git checkout.
outputs: Go module and versioned registry resolver.
CLI or native entry adapter accepting machine-readable contract lookup and validation operations.
Error taxonomy for unresolved, invalid, incompatible and supported cases.
acceptance: No fixed src/ptsip path required at runtime.
No dependency edge from customer Go module to developer-only engine.
Missing or ambiguous URNs fail closed and do not guess versions.

work_units.title: Implement structural and semantic-extension compatibility evaluation in Go
inputs: Machine-verifiable semantic declarations and test vectors
actions: Separate reference resolution, JSON Schema structural validation, declared semantic constraints, and change-impact checks into distinct results.
Check that developer extension preserves common constraints; allow extra fields and compatible strengthening.
Treat unsupported or unprovable semantic comparison as UNRESOLVED, not compatible; reject demonstrated conflicts only in affected scope.
Record contract identity/revision, evidence and field/constraint pointers in a deterministic machine report.
Provide regression tests for same-name different-meaning, weakened restrictions, conflict, valid extension and independent unaffected contracts.
outputs: Go structural/semantic evaluation API and CLI.
Machine-readable conflict report with exact evidence and proof scope.
Positive/negative/unknown test fixtures.
acceptance: Structural VALID is never treated as proof of semantic equivalence.
Known weakening and contradiction rejected, unknown semantic equivalence unresolved.
Independent unaffected contracts remain independently eligible.

work_units.title: Replace old Python customer contract feature and update all callers
inputs: WU-01 exact call graph and golden outputs
New Go resolver, validator and source fidelity APIs
actions: Port required customer-facing unified contract behaviors to Go including read-only source restoration, canonical digest verification and currently depended-on contract validation.
Replace setup.py run_path() build-time dependency on src/ptsip/policy_contracts/unified.py with an exact Go-backed projection/build adapter before deleting the file.
Update developer Go contract authoring bridge to use the new independent Go behavior rather than executing the Python unified policy feature.
Update developer migration utility and governance/test callers that import the old module; preserve correct authority/validation boundaries.
Delete src/ptsip/policy_contracts/unified.py only after exact caller parity and package build succeed; eliminate empty obsolete package exports only if callsite analysis confirms safe.
Do not migrate unrelated Python application or packaging code absent direct customer contract feature responsibility.
outputs: Legacy customer Python contract feature removed.
All discovered former callers switched to Go or equivalent direct Go-backed adapter.
No stale module import in source, CI or wheel.
acceptance: All identified old customer contract behavior has verified Go replacement or an explicit out-of-scope disposition.
No remaining runnable dependency on ptsip.policy_contracts.unified.
Setup/build policy projection, source-preservation, developer policy authoring and verifier regressions pass.

work_units.title: Package Go executable and customer resources in installed PTSIP
inputs: Existing PEP 517 build and release backend
actions: Integrate Go build artifacts with current PTSIP wheel/sdist assembly, without replacing existing unrelated official Rust engine composition.
Install resources under ptsip/common_contract/schemas and a discoverable Go executable next to its package resources; avoid checkout-relative assumptions.
Make resource manifest revision and binary provenance verifiable in built artifacts.
Test an isolated Windows venv with .venv/Lib/site-packages/ptsip, plus Linux/macOS package environments, without assuming identical filesystem layouts.
Ensure no runtime import or bundling of old Python customer contract feature.
outputs: Wheel/sdist integration modifications and distributable Go customer contract runtime.
Installed-package manifest and exact asset verification.
acceptance: Wheel has six declared schemas and working platform-matched Go binary.
Standalone installed environment resolves all six URNs and validates status enum without repository checkout.
No developer Go engine install required for customer runtime.

work_units.title: Register scoped verification and repair known missing-test guard
inputs: src/tests/ptsip/contracts (currently absent; referenced by existing workflows)
actions: Add precise Go-unit and installed wheel acceptance tests for all approved policy rule obligations.

Resolve pre-existing policy-contract guard missing-test paths by adding maintained replacement tests or updating obsolete targets only after coverage parity, rather than skipping contract verification.
Register or adjust the narrowest relevant mode in .github/test_modes.yaml; keep tooling-test.yml a stable verification executor and modify only if required.
Test negative cases for absent resource, ambiguous URN, developer status schema contamination, semantic weakening, unknown semantics, and stale installer assets.
Capture deterministic report artifacts and logs; never commit local log files.
outputs: Go conformance fixtures and cross-platform installation smoke tests.
Updated scoped test mode and repaired policy contract guard coverage.
Machine-readable verification evidence.
acceptance: All six rule IDs have at least one explicit conformance test.
Local Go tests, static checks, build and installed-wheel smoke tests pass.
Relevant GitHub Actions complete on exact pushed SHA; no blanket all-mode run when scoped mode suffices.
Pre-existing missing src/tests/ptsip/contracts/test_unified_policy.py and test_migrate_unified_current.py references no longer cause a missing-test failure.

work_units.title: Final dependency-free installed runtime and release readiness review
actions: Verify no packaging, build, developer tooling or customer callsite still requires removed Python feature.
Compare exact released-source and built-asset integrity without asserting publication or release approval.
Record residual migration compatibility risks and any independently blocked scope; escalate new policy domain instead of silently deciding.
Prepare implementation report and await separate publication authorization as applicable.
outputs: Policy-to-test traceability report.
Go migration verification and release handoff report.
acceptance: No old Python customer feature is shipped or required.
All six resources are version resolved inside installed ptsip, all thirteen statuses supported, Go-only evaluator proves intended compatibility behavior.
No branch is created; no publication or release version silently selected.

pre_implementation: User reviews and approves the complete plan.
An admitted current plan contract and registration route is identified; do not misrepresent .ptsip/contracts/Plans/ field-review candidates as approved.
Current applicable policies are re-read at latest HEAD; conflicts escalated rather than overridden.
No obsolete developer release WU becomes this plan's implementation authority by proximity.
pre_python_removal: WU-04 Go contract feature parity proven
Existing build/authoring/migration callsites moved off old Python feature
pre_wheel_distribution: All six resources and manifest installed
Go binary packaged for target platform
Exact source and package asset integrity checked
pre_publication: Separate release/version/publication authorization and evidence as required

local_windows_11_in_order: Install built wheel in a fresh test venv; invoke its installed Go binary using package resource lookup; append output to $log
Remove the untracked log after communicating verification results
verification.preexisting_ci_issue: Policy contract guard references missing src/tests/ptsip/contracts/test_unified_policy.py and test_migrate_unified_current.py; repair covered in WU-07.
